_comment: The film's script (PLAN.md §3), in film order. Phase 1 holds the test shots only. keyframes.first/last are Qwen prompts (the shot's look is appended); video is H3's [Shot 1] text without the alignment line, which make_clips.py adds; facts name entries in FACTS.md.

keyframes.first: Aerial view of the White House in Washington, D.C., in the summer of 1955, filmed from a low-flying aircraft high above Lafayette Square, looking south. In the foreground, Pennsylvania Avenue with a few rounded 1950s cars, and beyond its iron fence the wide, deep North Lawn with its round fountain and a semicircular asphalt driveway curving from two gates on Pennsylvania Avenue up to the columned North Portico and back. The white mansion stands well back from the street and is by far the largest and tallest building in view. On either side of it, much smaller, single-storey white wings sit low and half hidden among the trees: the West Wing on the right and the East Wing on the left, each joined to the house by a low colonnade. Beyond the house, open green parkland: the South Lawn, then the large green oval of the Ellipse, and behind it the Washington Monument rising alone from open grounds, no buildings in between. Warm late-afternoon sun, long soft shadows. Wide aerial shot looking down at an angle.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955, an aerial shot. The camera glides slowly forward over the White House shown in <Picture 1> and pans gently to the right, the mansion turning slowly beneath it; a few rounded 1950s cars drive along Pennsylvania Avenue.
shots.soundscape: Wind over an aircraft, the distant hum of city traffic far below. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: The White House press room in July 1955: a small crowded room with wood panelling and a window with venetian blinds. In the left foreground, seen from behind and out of focus, a man in a dark suit holds up a typed sheet of paper. Facing him, a tight crowd of reporters in suits, ties and fedoras, notebooks and pencils in hand, and press photographers raising large press cameras with round silver flash reflectors, the moment just before the first picture is taken: the room lit only by warm lamp light and the daylight through the blinds. Medium-wide shot at eye level, 35mm lens.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955. In the press room shown in <Picture 1>, the photographers take their pictures: each flashbulb fires as a single blink of white light that is gone in a split second, one camera at a time, now here, now there, like flashes in an old newsreel. The reporters scribble fast in their notebooks and lean in; one of them turns and hurries out of the room. The man in the foreground stays with his back to the camera, holding the typed sheet. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.
shots.soundscape: The pops and clicks of flashbulbs and press cameras, pencils scratching, the shuffle of a crowded room, a door opening. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: The White House press room in July 1955, a small room with wood panelling. In the left foreground, seen from behind and out of focus, a man in a dark suit holds up a typed sheet of paper. Facing him, close to the camera and in sharp focus, a small group of reporters in suits and ties: on the left, a stocky reporter in a grey fedora with a notebook open, pencil ready; in the middle, a thin bald reporter in glasses leaning forward to read the sheet; on the right, a press photographer in shirtsleeves raising a large press camera with a round silver flash reflector; between them two more reporters with notebooks. Behind the group, the rest of the room is a soft, heavily blurred background of warm lamp light and dark shapes. The room lit by warm lamp light and daylight through venetian blinds, no flash fired yet. Medium close shot at eye level, 85mm lens wide open, very shallow depth of field.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955. In the press room shown in <Picture 1>, the stocky reporter in the grey fedora taps his pencil twice on his notebook, then writes fast, his eyes on the sheet. The bald reporter in glasses leans in closer to read the sheet, then straightens up and turns to his neighbour. The photographer on the right fires his flashbulb once: a single blink of white light that is gone in a split second. One of the other reporters snaps his notebook shut, turns and hurries out of the frame. The man in the foreground stays with his back to the camera, holding the typed sheet. The background stays soft and blurred. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.
shots.soundscape: The pops and clicks of flashbulbs and press cameras, pencils scratching, the shuffle of a crowded room, a door opening. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Extreme close-up of a typed press statement held in a man's hand in 1955: a sheet of white paper typed on a typewriter, the line "small earth-circling satellites" sharp and clearly legible across the middle of the frame, the typed lines above and below it softly out of focus. The man's thumb and the cuff of a dark suit sleeve at the edge of the sheet. Warm light, a faint white glare of a flashbulb on the paper. Macro lens, very shallow depth of field.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955. The typed sheet shown in <Picture 1> trembles very slightly in the man's hand. A flashbulb flares white across the paper once. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the typed line, which stays sharp and still.
shots.soundscape: A flashbulb popping, the rustle of paper, a murmuring room behind. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Aerial view of the Moscow Kremlin in the summer of 1955, filmed from a low-flying aircraft: the long red brick walls and towers crowned with red stars, the golden onion domes of the cathedrals inside the walls, the Moskva River running along the front with an embankment, Red Square at one side with the colourful domes of Saint Basil's Cathedral, the city of 1950s Moscow beyond under a pale hazy sky. Wide aerial shot looking down at an angle.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955, an aerial shot. The camera glides slowly along the river past the Kremlin shown in <Picture 1> and pans gently to the left, the towers and golden domes turning slowly beneath it.
shots.soundscape: Wind over an aircraft, the distant hum of the city far below. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Close-up of a 1950s news-agency teleprinter in a Moscow office, 1955: a bulky dark grey machine on a metal stand, its rounded sheet-metal hood with a small glass window over the printing mechanism, a wide continuous roll of pale yellow paper rising out of a slot in the top of the hood and curling over the back. The printed line "США ЗАПУСТЯТ ИСКУССТВЕННЫЙ СПУТНИК ЗЕМЛИ" in Russian typewriter capitals is clearly legible on the paper just above the slot. Behind it, more teleprinters in a row along the wall of a news room. Hard window light from the left, dust in the air, a glass of tea in a metal holder on a shelf beside the machine. 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, the paper in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955. The teleprinter shown in <Picture 1> clatters and the yellow paper rises slowly out of the hood. A man's hand in a white shirt sleeve enters the frame from the right, grips the paper above the printed line and tears it off sharply against the hood's edge. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: The loud mechanical clatter of a teleprinter printing, a small bell ringing once, then the sharp rip of paper being torn. A quiet office around it. Nobody speaks.

subtitle.text: U.S. to launch an artificial Earth satellite

keyframes.first: A crowded press conference in Moscow in August 1955, a high-ceilinged hall with tall windows and heavy curtains. In the foreground, seen from behind and slightly to the side, a Soviet scientist in a grey suit sits at a table covered with green cloth, a bank of old chrome microphones in front of him; only the back of his head and his shoulders are visible. Facing him across the room, about fifty journalists in suits sit and stand packed together, notebooks open, pencils raised, a few press photographers with cameras. Hard daylight from the windows. Wide shot from behind the scientist, 35mm lens.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955. In the hall shown in <Picture 1>, the scientist in the foreground stays with his back to the camera and leans toward the microphones. Across the room the journalists' pencils stop; they stare at him in silence. Then several of them jump up and push toward the door while others write furiously. The camera holds a static shot from behind the scientist.
shots.soundscape: A crowded hall falling silent, then chairs scraping, a rush of footsteps toward the door and an excited murmur of many voices, no words intelligible. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: An American engineering office at night in 1955. On the right of the frame, a cork board on the wall covered with technical drawings, next to a blackboard with a chalk sketch of the Earth and an elliptical orbit around it. On the left, an engineer seen from behind, in a white short-sleeved shirt and a narrow dark tie, his raised hand pinning a newspaper clipping to the cork board; the clipping's headline "SOVIETS PLAN SATELLITE TOO" in bold newspaper type is clearly legible. Between the engineer and the cork board, in the corner, a large American flag of the 1950s, the Stars and Stripes, hangs from a wooden flagpole with a gold eagle on top, its red and white stripes and the white stars on the blue canton clearly visible in the lamp light. On a shelf above the cork board, an American football and a college pennant. A drafting table in the foreground with a green-shaded banker's lamp, a slide rule, a coffee mug and an ashtray. Warm lamp light, the windows dark. Medium shot, 50mm lens.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955. In the office shown in <Picture 1>, the engineer presses the pin into the clipping with his thumb, then lowers his hand and steps back to look at it, still with his back to the camera. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the clipping.
shots.soundscape: A quiet office at night: a ticking wall clock, the soft press of a pin into cork. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: A Soviet design bureau at night in 1955. On the right of the frame, a large board on the wall covered with technical drawings and a big hand-drawn sketch of a rocket with labels in Russian Cyrillic letters. On the left, an engineer seen from behind, in a white shirt with rolled-up sleeves, his raised hand pinning a clipping from a Soviet newspaper to the board; the clipping's headline "США ЗАПУСТЯТ ИСКУССТВЕННЫЙ СПУТНИК ЗЕМЛИ" in bold Russian newspaper type. In the corner beside the board, a large red Soviet flag with the golden hammer and sickle and the gold-bordered star in its upper corner hangs from a flagpole. Above the board, a red propaganda poster with a big golden hammer and sickle. A heavy wooden desk in the foreground with an unlit metal desk lamp, a glass of tea in a metal holder and a slide rule. Cold blue moonlight from a tall window, the room dim. Medium shot, 50mm lens.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955. In the room shown in <Picture 1>, the engineer presses the pin into the clipping with his thumb, then reaches down and switches on the desk lamp: warm light floods the board and the rocket sketch. He stays with his back to the camera. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the board.
shots.soundscape: A quiet room at night: the soft press of a pin, the click of a lamp switch. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Close-up of a tear-off day calendar hanging on the wood-panelled wall of an American office in the 1950s: a thick block of thin paper pages clipped to a printed cardboard backing. The top page shows the date in large bold black print, clearly legible: "AUGUST" across the top, a huge numeral "2" in the middle, "1955" and "TUESDAY" below it. Warm desk-lamp light from the side, the wall softly out of focus around the calendar. The calendar fills the centre of the frame, 85mm lens, the page in sharp focus.
keyframes.last: Close-up of a tear-off day calendar hanging on the wood-panelled wall of an American office in the 1950s: a thick block of thin paper pages clipped to a printed cardboard backing. The top page shows the date in large bold black print, clearly legible: "OCTOBER" across the top, a huge numeral "4" in the middle, "1957" and "FRIDAY" below it. Warm desk-lamp light from the side, the wall softly out of focus around the calendar. The calendar fills the centre of the frame, 85mm lens, the page in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957. The pages of the calendar shown in <Picture 1> tear off by themselves one after another and fly away out of the frame, slowly at first, then faster and faster, a flutter of paper like a time-lapse in an old film, until the tearing stops and the calendar settles on the page shown in <Picture 2>. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: Paper tearing and fluttering, slowly at first and then faster and faster, then it stops; a clock ticking in a quiet office. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: An evening reception in the ballroom of an embassy in Washington, October 1957. Crystal chandeliers, tall windows with heavy curtains, a long buffet table with white linen, waiters carrying silver trays of champagne coupes. In the middle ground a grey-haired American scientist in his fifties, in a dark suit and tie, holds a champagne coupe, while a younger man in a rumpled grey suit leans in close to whisper into his ear, one hand half raised. Around them small groups of men in dark suits and a few women in cocktail dresses talk, softly out of focus. Medium shot at eye level, 50mm lens.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957. In the embassy ballroom shown in <Picture 1>, the younger man in the grey suit whispers urgently into the grey-haired scientist's ear. The scientist's polite smile fades. He slowly lowers his champagne coupe and turns his head to look at the younger man, stunned, then glances across the room. Around them the reception carries on, unaware. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the two men.
shots.soundscape: The murmur of a crowded evening reception, glasses clinking softly, distant polite laughter, no words intelligible. Nobody in frame speaks aloud.

keyframes.first: The ballroom of an embassy in Washington during an evening reception, October 1957. Over the shoulder of a grey-haired scientist in a dark suit, seen from behind and softly out of focus in the left foreground, his right hand raising a champagne coupe. Facing him and the camera, a crowd of guests in dark suits and a few women in cocktail dresses, glasses in hand, their faces lit warmly by the chandeliers. The Americans in the front rows look stiff and unsettled, mouths set in tight polite smiles; two Soviet diplomats in the middle of the crowd beam openly. Crystal chandeliers, wood panelling and red curtains behind them. Medium-wide shot at eye level, 50mm lens, the crowd's faces in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957. In the ballroom shown in <Picture 1>, the grey-haired scientist in the foreground lifts his champagne coupe a little higher in a toast. Facing him, the guests slowly raise their glasses in answer. The two Soviet diplomats smile broadly and lift their glasses high. The Americans raise theirs reluctantly, only to shoulder height, with tight, forced smiles; one of them glances sideways at his neighbour, another stares into his glass before drinking. The mood is subdued and awkward, a polite toast to a rival's success. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the front row of faces.
shots.soundscape: A large room that has fallen quiet: a single glass being tapped, a few murmurs, the shuffle of feet, then sparse, hesitant applause from a few people. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: The ballroom of an embassy in Washington during an evening reception, October 1957. Over the shoulder of a grey-haired scientist in a dark suit, seen from behind and out of focus in the left foreground, his right hand raising a champagne coupe in a toast. Facing him, close to the camera and in sharp focus, a small group of six guests: in the middle, two Soviet diplomats in grey double-breasted suits with small red lapel badges, beaming, their champagne coupes raised high; on the left, a heavyset American official in a dark suit with empty hands and his arms folded, his jaw set, unsmiling; next to him a silver-haired American in a dark suit holding his coupe low at his chest, a thin, fixed smile; on the right, a young American engineer with horn-rimmed glasses and empty hands, his eyes lowered; beside him a woman in a dark cocktail dress, one gloved hand at her pearls, glancing uneasily at the men beside her. Behind them the rest of the ballroom is a soft, heavily blurred background of chandelier light and dark shapes. Medium shot at eye level, 85mm lens wide open, very shallow depth of field.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957. In the ballroom shown in <Picture 1>, the beaming Soviet diplomat in the grey double-breasted suit in the middle lifts his coupe high and drinks, smiling broadly. The silver-haired American behind him raises his coupe only a few inches, his smile thin and fixed, and takes a small sip. The heavyset American on the left slowly unfolds his arms and claps twice, slowly, without smiling. The young man with glasses on the right keeps his coupe low and does not drink, his face blank. The woman on the far right glances from one man to the other, her gloved hand at her pearls. The grey-haired man in the foreground keeps his glass raised. The background stays soft and blurred. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.
shots.soundscape: A large room that has fallen quiet: two slow, isolated hand claps; a glass clinking once; a faint murmur far away. Nobody speaks.

subjects: <Subject 1>: the satellite shown in <Picture 1>, a polished metal sphere with four long thin straight antennas that all sweep backward from one side of the sphere.
shots.summary: The target video shows <Subject 1> in orbit high above the Earth.
retention: <Picture 1> ([Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the satellite's shape is kept exactly: its mirror-polished sphere, its seams and its four swept-back antennas, no more and no fewer. The framing, the view of the Earth and the light are new.
shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, photorealistic, as if filmed by a camera in Earth orbit: pure black space with no stars, hard unfiltered sunlight. <Subject 1> flies forward from left to right across the upper half of the frame, the polished sphere leading and its four antennas trailing straight behind it to the left. A single Earth fills the lower part of the frame, its curved horizon steady: oceans and clouds in daylight, the night side darkening toward the right. The camera tracks alongside <Subject 1> at its own speed, so the satellite stays near the centre while the Earth's surface slides slowly past beneath it, and the sunlight glints across its mirror surface.
shots.soundscape: A loud, clear, steady electronic beep from a shortwave radio receiver, two short beeps per second, with a soft crackle of radio static between them. The beeping is the main sound and is clearly audible throughout.

keyframes.first: The flat tar-paper rooftop of an American apartment building at dusk, October 1957. A few neighbours in ordinary 1950s autumn clothes, everyone in long trousers or a long skirt, stand together near the parapet, looking up at the darkening sky: on the left, a man in a white shirt with rolled-up sleeves, long dark trousers and suspenders holds a small portable radio up toward the sky with both hands; next to him a woman in a cardigan, one hand at her throat; in front of them a boy in a striped T-shirt and long trousers pointing upward; on the right, an older man in a cardigan and grey slacks with a pipe, shading his eyes. Behind them rooftops, television aerials and a water tower against a deep blue evening sky, the last orange glow on the horizon and the first stars. Medium-wide shot from a low angle, 35mm lens.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957. On the rooftop shown in <Picture 1>, the man raises the little radio higher toward the sky. High above, a small bright point of light moves slowly and steadily across the darkening sky from left to right. The boy follows it with his pointing finger; the woman slowly lowers her hand from her throat; the older man takes the pipe out of his mouth and stares. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: A small radio speaker playing a clear electronic beep, two short beeps per second, with crackling static; a quiet evening city far below, a dog barking in the distance. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.last: Close-up of a tear-off day calendar hanging on the wood-panelled wall of an American office in the 1950s: a thick block of thin paper pages clipped to a printed cardboard backing. The top page shows the date in large bold black print, clearly legible: "DECEMBER" across the top, a huge numeral "6" in the middle, "1957" and "FRIDAY" below it. Warm desk-lamp light from the side, the wall softly out of focus around the calendar. The calendar fills the centre of the frame, 85mm lens, the page in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957. The pages of the calendar shown in <Picture 1> tear off by themselves one after another and fly away out of the frame, slowly at first, then faster and faster, a flutter of paper like a time-lapse in an old film, until the tearing stops and the calendar settles on the page shown in <Picture 2>. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: Paper tearing and fluttering, slowly at first and then faster and faster, then it stops; a clock ticking in a quiet office. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Cape Canaveral, Florida, late morning on 6 December 1957, Launch Complex 18A: the Vanguard rocket, a very slim white rocket about 22 metres tall, as tall as a seven-storey building, and only about a metre wide, stands upright on a steel launch stand on a concrete pad, a thin wisp of white vapour venting from its side. Just beside it a slender umbilical mast with cables running to the rocket; a short distance behind it a huge red-and-white steel service gantry, taller than the rocket, rolled back on rails. Two small figures of technicians in white coveralls walk away from the base of the rocket, their heads barely reaching the bottom of its first stage. Flat sandy scrubland with low palmetto bushes around the pad, a pale clear sky. Seen from a few hundred metres away across the scrub, as by a newsreel camera, 85mm telephoto lens, the whole rocket and gantry in frame.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957, newsreel footage. At the launch pad shown in <Picture 1>, the two technicians in white coveralls in front of the mast walk briskly away to the right and out of the frame, and the lone figure on the far left walks off to the left and out of the frame, leaving the pad empty. Then the slim white rocket ignites: fire and white smoke burst from its base and it lifts only slightly, barely a metre off the launch stand, hesitates, loses its thrust and sinks back down; then it bursts into a huge orange fireball that swallows it from the bottom up, and its top section topples away from the flames. The red gantry and the mast stand untouched. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: The roar of a rocket engine igniting, sputtering, then a deep rolling explosion and debris falling, wind across the scrub. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Close to the ground in the sandy scrubland beside a launch pad at Cape Canaveral, December 1957. Black smoke drifts low across the frame from a fire burning in the background. In the foreground, among scorched palmetto bushes in the sand, lies a small dented metal sphere the size of a grapefruit with six thin straight antennas sticking out from it at odd angles, lying on its side. Low angle, 100mm lens, shallow depth of field, the little sphere in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957. In the scrub shown in <Picture 1>, black smoke drifts slowly across the frame, small flames flicker in the background and flakes of ash float down. The little sphere lies still on its side among the bushes. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the sphere.
shots.soundscape: A faint, steady electronic beep, two short beeps per second, coming from the little sphere; wind through the bushes and the crackle of a distant fire. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Close-up of a Soviet tear-off day calendar hanging on the plain painted wall of a Soviet office around 1960: a thick block of thin paper pages on a printed cardboard backing with a small red star. The top page shows the date in large bold print in Russian Cyrillic letters, clearly legible: "ОКТЯБРЬ" in red across the top, a huge red numeral "4" in the middle, "1957" and "ПЯТНИЦА" below it in black. Cold daylight from a window at the side, the wall softly out of focus around the calendar. The calendar fills the centre of the frame, 85mm lens, the page in sharp focus.
keyframes.last: Close-up of a Soviet tear-off day calendar hanging on the plain painted wall of a Soviet office around 1960: a thick block of thin paper pages on a printed cardboard backing with a small red star. The top page shows the date in large bold print in Russian Cyrillic letters, clearly legible: "АПРЕЛЬ" in red across the top, a huge red numeral "12" in the middle, "1961" and "СРЕДА" below it in black. Cold daylight from a window at the side, the wall softly out of focus around the calendar. The calendar fills the centre of the frame, 85mm lens, the page in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1961. The pages of the calendar shown in <Picture 1> tear off by themselves one after another and fly away out of the frame, slowly at first, then faster and faster, a flutter of paper like a time-lapse in an old film, until the tearing stops and the calendar settles on the page shown in <Picture 2>. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: Paper tearing and fluttering, slowly at first and then faster and faster, then it stops; a clock ticking in a quiet office. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Inside the cramped capsule of the Vostok spacecraft in orbit, 1961. A cosmonaut seen in profile from the side, filling the right half of the frame: a white spherical pressure helmet with the four red Cyrillic letters "СССР" painted large across its forehead, its clear visor closed. In the visor, a bright reflection of the blue Earth and white clouds from a small round porthole beside him; behind the reflection his face is lost in shadow. The orange collar of his spacesuit, padded straps across his shoulder. Around him, the curved wall of the capsule with a few dials and switches in pale grey. Cold blue light from the porthole, deep shadows. Close-up, 50mm lens.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1961. Inside the capsule shown in <Picture 1>, from the very first moment the cosmonaut in the white helmet slowly lifts his head and turns it toward the round porthole on the left, a slow, steady turn that carries on through the whole shot until he looks out at the Earth. The clouds and blue ocean drift slowly across the porthole, and their blue light slides across his clear visor and the white helmet as he turns. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the helmet.
shots.soundscape: The low hum of fans inside a small capsule, a faint crackle of radio static, the soft creak of a spacesuit. Nobody speaks.

subjects: <Subject 1>: the spacecraft shown in <Picture 1>, a grey metal sphere joined to a ribbed cone-shaped equipment module, a ring of small round tanks around the joint between them and a few thin antennas.
shots.summary: The target video shows <Subject 1> in orbit high above the Earth.
retention: <Picture 1> ([Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the spacecraft's shape is kept exactly: its grey sphere, the ring of round tanks, the ribbed cone and its thin antennas. The framing, the view of the Earth and the light are new.
shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, photorealistic, as if filmed by a camera in Earth orbit: pure black space with no stars, hard unfiltered sunlight. <Subject 1> flies forward from left to right across the upper half of the frame, its sphere leading and the ribbed cone trailing behind it. A single Earth fills the lower part of the frame, its curved horizon steady: oceans, land and clouds in daylight. The camera tracks alongside <Subject 1> at its own speed, so it stays near the centre while the Earth's surface slides slowly past beneath it, and the sunlight glints across the metal.
shots.soundscape: A soft, low electronic hum. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Inside a bright American aerospace hangar in April 1961, seen from just behind two engineers standing shoulder to shoulder, the camera looking over their shoulders. Together they hold an open newspaper up in front of them at chest height, the man on the left in a white short-sleeved shirt holding its left edge, the man on the right in a white lab coat holding its right edge; both their heads are bent over it, seen from behind. The front page faces the camera over their shoulders, its headline in huge bold black capitals: "SOVIET MAN IN SPACE". Beyond the newspaper, out of focus in the middle of the hangar, a half-assembled Mercury space capsule stands on a work stand: a small black cone-shaped capsule with ribbed metal shingles, panels open, cables hanging from it. Work lights overhead, a concrete floor. Over-the-shoulder medium close-up, 50mm lens, the headline in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1961. In the hangar shown in <Picture 1>, the two engineers hold the newspaper perfectly still between them and read. The man on the right slowly shakes his head and rubs the back of his neck with his free hand. The man on the left slowly lifts his head from the paper and looks up at the unfinished capsule beyond it. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: A large hangar: an electric drill whirring in the distance, the hum of overhead lights, a toolbox set down on concrete. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Cape Canaveral, Florida, the clear morning of 5 May 1961, seen from a few hundred metres away: a Mercury-Redstone rocket stands upright on a small square steel launch stand on a flat concrete pad. The rocket is a plain white cylinder about twenty-five metres tall with the words "UNITED STATES" in black running down its side and four small fins at its base. On its top sits a small black cone-shaped Mercury capsule, and above the capsule a slim red steel lattice escape tower with a small rocket on its tip. Far off to the right, a tall red steel service gantry stands rolled away along its rails. Flat sandy ground with low green scrub, a pale blue morning sky. A telephoto newsreel view, 200mm lens, the whole rocket in the frame from the pad to the tip of its tower.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1961, newsreel footage. The slim white rocket shown in <Picture 1>, with its black and white capsule and red escape tower on top, stands on the pad beside the red service tower. It ignites: a bright flame and clouds of white smoke burst from its base and spread across the pad, and it rises slowly off the pad and climbs straight up into the blue sky on a short, bright, steady flame. The camera tilts up slowly to follow it.
shots.soundscape: The roar of a rocket engine igniting and building, a long thundering rumble, wind. Nobody speaks.
shots._comment: First frame: references/redstone_frame.png (the user's Redstone rocket program art, cropped to 16:9), picked by the user.

subjects: <Subject 1>: the spacecraft shown in <Picture 1>, a small black cone-shaped capsule with ribbed metal shingles, "UNITED STATES" and an American flag painted on its side, a narrow cylinder on its nose and a round heat shield with a small rocket pack strapped to its wide end.
shots.summary: The target video shows <Subject 1> in orbit high above the Pacific Ocean.
retention: <Picture 1> ([Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the capsule's shape is kept exactly: its black shingled cone, the lettering and flag, the nose cylinder and the rocket pack on its heat shield. The framing, the view of the Earth and the light are new.
shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, photorealistic, as if filmed by a camera in Earth orbit: pure black space with no stars, hard unfiltered sunlight. <Subject 1> drifts slowly across the upper half of the frame from right to left, its wide heat shield leading, and sunlight flares off its ribbed shingles. A single Earth fills the lower part of the frame: the deep blue Pacific Ocean with scattered white clouds, its curved horizon steady. The camera tracks alongside <Subject 1> at its own speed while the ocean slides slowly past far below.
shots.soundscape: A soft, low electronic hum. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Rice Stadium in Houston, Texas, on a hot sunny afternoon in September 1962, seen from behind the speaker's lectern on a stage at the edge of the field. In the foreground on the left, the back and shoulders of a man in a dark suit with short brown hair, standing at a wooden lectern with several microphones on it and a few typed pages on its top. Beyond him, the huge open stadium stands packed with thousands of people in light summer clothes, many in white shirts, some shading their eyes, under a bright blue sky with harsh sunlight. The crowd is a soft blur of white and pastel. Medium shot over the shoulder, 50mm lens, the man's back and the lectern in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1962. In the stadium shown in <Picture 1>, the man in the dark suit at the wooden lectern on the left stands in silence, raises his right hand and brings it down firmly once in a gesture of emphasis, then rests it on the lectern. He stays with his back to the camera. The packed stands beyond him sit still and listen in the bright sun. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the lectern.
shots.soundscape: The low, steady murmur of a huge open-air crowd waiting in silence on a hot afternoon, a soft breeze across the microphones. The man at the lectern is silent. No one speaks; no voices, no words.

keyframes.first: The stands of Rice Stadium in Houston on a hot sunny afternoon in September 1962, a few rows of people seated close to the camera, listening to a speech: on the left, a middle-aged man in a white short-sleeved shirt and a straw hat shading his eyes with a folded paper programme; in the middle, a woman in a light summer dress and sunglasses holding a paper fan; on the right, a young student in shirtsleeves, elbows on his knees, leaning forward. Behind them the rest of the crowd is a soft blur of white shirts and pastel colours. Harsh bright sunlight. Medium shot, 85mm lens wide open, the three people in sharp focus and the background blurred.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1962. In the stands shown in <Picture 1>, the man in the straw hat on the left lifts the programme from his lap and slowly fans himself with it. The woman in sunglasses in the middle fans herself with her folded paper, then stops and holds it still in her lap. The young man on the right, elbows on his knees, clasps his hands together and leans further forward. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: A huge open-air stadium on a hot afternoon: a large attentive crowd, quiet; a breeze; the rustle of paper fans. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: The open Kazakh steppe on a bright June day in 1963, flat grassland under a huge pale blue sky with a few white clouds. In the foreground on the right, seen from behind, a young woman cosmonaut stands in a bulky orange spacesuit; she has taken off her helmet and holds the white spherical helmet with the red letters "СССР" by her side in her right hand; her short dark wavy hair stirs in the wind. Beside her on the grass lies a large crumpled orange and white parachute. Ahead of her in the middle distance, a few villagers in simple work clothes and headscarves hurry across the grass toward her, small figures; one man raises his cap in greeting. Medium-wide shot from behind her shoulder, 50mm lens.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1963. On the steppe shown in <Picture 1>, the woman in the orange spacesuit stays with her back to the camera and raises her free left hand high to wave to the villagers ahead, the white helmet still hanging from her right hand. The wind lifts her dark hair and ripples the parachute lying on the grass. The villagers hurry closer across the field, one of them waving his arm. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward her.
shots.soundscape: Wind across open grassland, the parachute fabric flapping, distant faint shouts of greeting. Nobody speaks close by.

subjects: <Subject 1>: the cosmonaut shown in <Picture 1>, in a white spacesuit with a white helmet, joined by a long thin tether to the spacecraft shown in <Picture 1>, a metal sphere with a long cylindrical airlock tube sticking out of its side.
shots.summary: The target video shows <Subject 1> floating outside the spacecraft high above the Earth.
retention: <Picture 1> ([Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the white spacesuit, the tether and the spacecraft's sphere and airlock tube are kept exactly. The framing, the view of the Earth and the light are new.
shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, photorealistic, as if filmed by a camera in Earth orbit: pure black space with no stars, hard unfiltered sunlight. <Subject 1> drifts slowly away from the end of the airlock tube, arms spread, the thin tether curving gently behind him back to the spacecraft. A single Earth fills the lower part of the frame, huge and blue with white clouds, its curved horizon steady. He turns slowly in the sunlight. The camera drifts slowly around him.
shots.soundscape: Slow, steady breathing inside a helmet and a soft electronic hum.

subjects: <Subject 1>: the small dark cone-shaped spacecraft shown on the right of <Picture 1>.
<Subject 2>: the long silver cylindrical target vehicle shown on the left of <Picture 1>, with a round docking collar on its end.
shots.summary: The target video shows <Subject 1> docking with <Subject 2> in orbit high above the Earth.
retention: <Picture 1> ([Shot 1]): partially_preserved - both spacecraft are kept exactly: the dark cone of <Subject 1> and the long silver cylinder and docking collar of <Subject 2>. In the first moment they are a few metres apart; the framing, the view of the Earth and the light are new.
shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, photorealistic, as if filmed by a camera in Earth orbit: pure black space with no stars, hard unfiltered sunlight. <Subject 1> approaches <Subject 2> slowly and steadily, nose first, from a few metres away, and its narrow nose slides gently into the docking collar on the end of <Subject 2> until the two spacecraft touch and lock together. A single Earth fills the lower part of the frame, blue and white, its curved horizon steady. The camera holds a steady view from the side.
shots.soundscape: A soft electronic hum, then a single dull metallic clunk as the two spacecraft lock together.

keyframes.first: An American rocket engine test stand at night in the mid-1960s: a towering steel test stand lit by floodlights, with a huge rocket engine bell mounted at its base firing straight down into a concrete flame trench. A blinding white column of flame roars out of the engine and billows out sideways in enormous clouds of white smoke and steam lit orange from within. In the foreground, a chain-link fence and a low concrete bunker. Wide shot from a distance, 85mm lens, the flame the brightest thing in the frame.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1965. At the test stand shown in <Picture 1>, the huge engine bell held in the stand keeps firing straight down: the blinding flame hits the flame deflector at the foot of the stand and blasts out sideways in a long horizontal stream of fire and smoke across the ground, and the clouds of smoke and steam boil and billow outward faster and faster, lit orange from within. The stand stays fixed in place. The ground and the camera shake. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: The deafening, crackling roar of a giant rocket engine at full thrust, a deep rumble that shakes everything. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: An American mission control room in 1966, calm and quiet: rows of grey consoles with small screens and banks of switches, a soft haze of cigarette smoke under the ceiling lights, a big clock on the wall. In the foreground, two controllers in white short-sleeved shirts and thin dark ties at a console, seen from the side: on the left, one leans back in his chair with his hands clasped behind his head; on the right, the other holds a cigarette to his lips and a lit match in his other hand. On the console in front of them, a single round indicator lamp glows steady green. The rest of the room behind them is a soft blur of consoles and shapes. Medium shot, 85mm lens wide open.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1966. In the control room shown in <Picture 1>, all is calm: the man leaning back keeps his hands behind his head; the other lights his cigarette and shakes out the match. The green lamp on the console glows steadily. Then, near the end, the lamp suddenly turns bright red, and the man leaning back sits bolt upright and stares at it. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: A calm, quiet control room: the hum of equipment, a clock ticking, a match struck; then a single sharp electronic warning tone. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Arlington National Cemetery, Virginia, on a grey winter afternoon in 1967: in the foreground, a round funeral wreath of white carnations and green leaves on a low stand before a plain white marble headstone seen from the side, its face turned away from the camera. Beyond it, rows and rows of identical white headstones run in straight lines across a gently sloping lawn of pale winter grass, softly out of focus, with bare trees on the hill. Soft grey light, very quiet and still, a moment of mourning. 85mm lens wide open, shallow depth of field, the wreath in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1967. At the wreath shown in <Picture 1>, nothing moves but a light cold breeze stirring the petals and the bare branches far behind, as the grey light slowly dims. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: Near silence: a soft cold wind, a few distant birds. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: The foot of the Kremlin Wall on Red Square in Moscow, on an overcast spring day in 1967: in the foreground, a large round funeral wreath of red carnations and dark green fir branches with a red ribbon leans against the base of the tall dark red brick wall, filling the lower half of the frame. Small dark granite memorial plaques set into the wall above it are softly out of focus. Grey cobblestones in front. Soft grey light, very quiet and still, a moment of mourning. 85mm lens wide open, shallow depth of field, the wreath in sharp focus.

shots.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1967. At the wreath shown in <Picture 1>, nothing moves but a light breeze stirring the red ribbon and the carnations against the old red wall. The camera holds a static shot.
shots.soundscape: Near silence: a soft wind, a faraway city murmur. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: Close-up of a 1950s news-agency teleprinter in a Moscow office, 1955: a bulky dark grey machine on a metal stand, its rounded sheet-metal hood with a small glass window over the printing mechanism, a wide continuous roll of pale yellow paper rising out of a slot in the top of the hood and curling over the back. The printed line "U.S. TO LAUNCH EARTH SATELLITE" in typewriter capitals is clearly legible on the paper just above the slot. Behind it, more teleprinters in a row along the wall of a news room. Hard window light from the left, dust in the air, a cold glass of tea in a metal holder on a shelf beside the machine. 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, the paper in sharp focus.

tests.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1955. The teleprinter shown in <Picture 1> clatters and the yellow paper rises slowly out of the hood. A man's hand in a white shirt sleeve enters the frame from the right, grips the paper above the printed line and tears it off sharply against the hood's edge. The camera holds a static shot.
tests.soundscape: The loud mechanical clatter of a teletype printing, a small bell ringing once, then the sharp rip of paper being torn. A quiet office around it. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: An evening reception in the ballroom of an embassy in Washington, October 1957. Crystal chandeliers, tall windows with heavy curtains, a long buffet table with white linen, waiters carrying silver trays of champagne coupes. In the middle ground a grey-haired American scientist in his fifties, in a dark suit and tie, holds a champagne coupe, while a younger man in a rumpled grey suit leans in close to whisper into his ear, one hand half raised. Around them small groups of men in dark suits and a few women in cocktail dresses talk, softly out of focus. Medium shot at eye level, 50mm lens.

tests.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957. In the embassy ballroom shown in <Picture 1>, the younger man in the grey suit whispers urgently into the grey-haired scientist's ear. The scientist's polite smile fades. He slowly lowers his champagne coupe and turns his head to look at the younger man, stunned, then glances across the room. Around them the reception carries on, unaware. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the two men.
tests.soundscape: The murmur of a crowded evening reception, glasses clinking softly, distant polite laughter, no words intelligible. Nobody in frame speaks aloud.

keyframes.first: The ballroom of an embassy in Washington during an evening reception, October 1957. Over the shoulder of a grey-haired scientist in a dark suit, seen from behind and softly out of focus in the left foreground, his right hand raising a champagne coupe. Facing him and the camera, a crowd of guests in dark suits and a few women in cocktail dresses, glasses in hand, their faces lit warmly by the chandeliers. The Americans in the front rows look stiff and unsettled, mouths set in tight polite smiles; two Soviet diplomats in the middle of the crowd beam openly. Crystal chandeliers, wood panelling and red curtains behind them. Medium-wide shot at eye level, 50mm lens, the crowd's faces in sharp focus.

tests.video: Live-action, cinematic, 1957. In the ballroom shown in <Picture 1>, the grey-haired scientist in the foreground lifts his champagne coupe a little higher in a toast. Facing him, the guests slowly raise their glasses in answer. The two Soviet diplomats smile broadly and lift their glasses high. The Americans raise theirs reluctantly, only to shoulder height, with tight, forced smiles; one of them glances sideways at his neighbour, another stares into his glass before drinking. The mood is subdued and awkward, a polite toast to a rival's success. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the front row of faces.
tests.soundscape: A large room that has fallen quiet: a single glass being tapped, a few murmurs, the shuffle of feet, then sparse, hesitant applause from a few people. Nobody speaks.

keyframes.first: A small polished metal sphere, about half a metre across, with four long thin straight antennas sweeping back from it in a narrow V, in orbit high above the Earth. The sphere's mirror-bright surface catches the sun and reflects the planet below. Beneath it the curved Earth at the edge of night: on one side oceans and clouds in daylight, on the other the darkened hemisphere. The sphere sits in the left third of the frame, seen slightly from below and behind.

tests.video: Live-action, cinematic. The polished satellite shown in <Picture 1> glides slowly across the frame from left to right high above the Earth, its four antennas trailing behind it, sunlight sliding across its mirror surface. Far below, the Earth turns slowly and the line between day and night creeps across the clouds. The camera tracks the satellite with small amplitude at slow speed.
tests.soundscape: Silence of space, broken only by a steady, thin electronic beep from a radio receiver, about two short beeps per second, slightly crackly.

subjects: <Subject 1>: the satellite shown in <Picture 1>, a polished metal sphere with four long thin straight antennas that all sweep backward from one side of the sphere.
tests.summary: The target video shows <Subject 1> in orbit high above the Earth.

tests.video: Live-action, cinematic, photorealistic, as if filmed by a camera in Earth orbit: pure black space with no stars, hard unfiltered sunlight. <Subject 1> flies forward from left to right across the upper half of the frame, the polished sphere leading and its four antennas trailing straight behind it to the left. A single Earth fills the lower part of the frame, its curved horizon steady: oceans and clouds in daylight, the night side darkening toward the right. The camera tracks alongside <Subject 1> at its own speed, so the satellite stays near the centre while the Earth's surface slides slowly past beneath it, and the sunlight glints across its mirror surface.
tests.soundscape: A loud, clear, steady electronic beep from a shortwave radio receiver, two short beeps per second, with a soft crackle of radio static between them. The beeping is the main sound and is clearly audible throughout.

tests.video: Live-action, cinematic, photorealistic. The polished satellite shown in <Picture 1> drifts slowly through orbit high above the Earth, its four antennas fixed rigidly in place. The camera arcs slowly around it with small amplitude, so the sunlight slides across its mirror surface and the Earth's horizon tilts gently behind it. The Earth below turns slowly, clouds drifting over the land.
tests.soundscape: Silence of space, broken only by a steady, thin electronic beep from a radio receiver, about two short beeps per second, slightly crackly.
